title: Every drag-and-drop action needs a keyboard path
rule: When a UI lets the user change structure by dragging (nest, reorder, move items into a group), give every outcome a drag can produce a keyboard-reachable control too: a row button or a palette command for each move (into, out of, up, down). Check that an outcome the keyboard can undo (Out) has a keyboard way back (In). Add a Playwright step that focuses the control and presses Enter, without dragTo, and asserts the new structure.
rationale: E7.1 (#82): nesting an existing collection was drag-only; the row buttons offered Up, Down and Out but nothing to nest into a sibling, so keyboard users could not nest and could not undo Out.
